task: Investigate current storage-selection errors related to historical upgrade report #2140; implement only independently proven picker error boundary after explicit Root authorization.

result.current_defect: Directory-picker exceptions are raised before the existing runCatching in both SetupActivity and ProfileSettingsFragment. StorageAccess 2.0.0 can resume the picker await with SecurityException or a provider/stat exception, so those errors escape the coroutine instead of the existing recoverable selection/import feedback.
result.implementation_status: Two uncommitted production files changed in dedicated worktree; no PR or push performed by this agent.
result.issue_linkage: Related #2140 only. The historical e09ac711 upgrade failure is not reproduced or claimed fixed.

pr2199.scope: Confirmation, cancellation and keeping mode unchanged until confirmation/selection for #2095; no picker-await exception boundary or historical #2140 reproducer. This new patch is based directly on a047, without #2199.

observations: Previously working external user data directory; first launch after update asked to choose a directory; choosing the original directory failed.
Reporter says LineageOS and GrapheneOS reproduce it; reboot did not help.
Reporter later says clearing application data fixed it.

screenshot.meaning: Generic Trime fallback modal: folder selection failed or was cancelled, mode falls back to app-specific storage. Background shows app-specific storage and no selected data folder. This does not identify which permission/import/deployment step failed. It is not the DocumentsUI restricted-folder banner.

fix(storage): stop forgetting the picked folder and its grant

meaning: cab86dcc intentionally recovers app-scoped directories after late media and separates completed storage choice from transient accessibility. Do not undo that design based on #2130 speculation.

675d7803 stops discarding the picked URI/grant before selection, on fallback, and after import failure; old e09ac711 can show the photographed fallback path, but its triggering exception remains unknown.
03a7380a updates StorageAccess to 2.0.0 and 1e4b9939 rewrites synchronization into UserDataManager. The current caller/library control flow differs from the reported historical release.

path: pickDirectory defaults to initialUri=null, writePermission=true, persistablePermission=true.
RESULT_OK and nonnull Intent: data!! -> takePersistableUriPermission(uri, READ|WRITE=3) -> StorageDocs.stat(context, uri). Returned Intent flags are not used to compute those permission bits.
parseResult catches Throwable and returns Result.failure; directoryLauncher resumes directoryContinuation with that Result; suspend caller receives the exception.
Both upstream UI callers await the picker before runCatching, so picker exceptions bypass existing failure handling.
library.null_result_path: Non-RESULT_OK or null Intent produces Result.success(null), the normal quiet cancellation path.

pure_jvm_evidence.scope: Verbatim function bodies extracted from current a047 and #2199, fake UI/storage dependencies, actual kotlinx.coroutines. This demonstrates control flow only; it is not Android/SAF/provider/upgrade execution or proof of an actual app crash.
pure_jvm_evidence.observation: Original a047 and #2199 Setup picker SecurityException/IOException reach the uncaught coroutine handler with no failure feedback and zero persistTreeUri calls. Moving the await into runCatching handles both; null and CancellationException stay quiet.

patch.summary: Reuse existing failure handling for directory picker exceptions and propagate coroutine cancellation in both UI entrypoints.
patch.setup: Move pickDirectory await inside existing runCatching. Keep null return quiet. Rethrow CancellationException before existing setup refresh/failure toast.
patch.profile: Capture the pending-first-enable flag before awaiting the picker, clear the internal pending flag, and use one lifecycleScope launch/runCatching covering picker and import. Remove the redundant second launch in the same scope. Null keeps existing silent cancellation behavior. Picker/import errors reuse first-enable APP_STORAGE fallback or reselect failure feedback. Rethrow CancellationException before changing mode, touching preferences or requesting context.
patch.saved_association_boundary: Before persistTreeUri is reached, this patch does not clear the saved URI, delete the sync manifest or release the old permission. A successful new grant followed by library stat failure can already have added a grant; this patch does not roll it back or claim all permissions remain unchanged.
patch.post_confirmation_sync_failure_boundary: PersistTreeUri and sync/deploy are unchanged. New URI/old grant/manifest mutations can precede sync failure; no transactional rollback is added or promised.
patch.logging: Existing feedback and exception boundary are reused; no new logging framework or broader diagnostic refactor.
patch.independence: No unmerged #2199 dependency. CancellationException rethrow overlaps a small part of that PR; same-function merge conflicts will need preserving both confirmation and this wider picker boundary.
patch.suggested_commit: fix(storage): handle folder picker failures without swallowing cancellation

regression.type: Pure JVM source extraction with fake Android/UI/storage dependencies and real coroutine cancellation
regression.matrix: upstream/fixed x (Setup, Settings-first-enable, Settings-reselect) x 9 cases = 54
cases: owner scope cancelled while picker suspended
owner scope cancelled while sync suspended
regression.outcome: All expected before/after assertions passed. Fixed picker errors reach existing feedback with zero persist/sync calls. First enable falls back to APP_STORAGE, reselect retains existing mode/saved URI. Null remains quiet. Direct or actual owner-scope cancellation avoids error UI and fallback; sync success/failure semantics remain modeled as before.
regression.baseline_lifecycle_observation: Cancelling the owner scope while sync is suspended triggers the old failure UI; first-enable Settings also falls back. The fixed extracted bodies rethrow CancellationException and perform no failure UI or fallback.
limitations: No actual FragmentActivity/PreferenceFragment/Dialog lifecycle or Android main thread is instantiated.
Fake UI records attempted calls after simulated destruction; it does not prove an Android lifecycle crash.
No real ContentResolver/provider/grant, manifest or file-byte state is asserted by this harness.
No checked-in test source or generic production helper was added, per Root direction; this repeatable diagnostic is retained under R.
regression.initial_harness_failure: First invocation compiled successfully but JVM classpath pointed to the old classes directory, so main class was not found (not a product error). Corrected runner passed; initial execution/stdout/stderr retained as harness-classpath-attempt1-*.

rejected_or_unproven_hypotheses.status: Unsupported. Confirmed-sync rollback is a separate limitation and explicitly outside this patch.
